requirements.says: Signing in and signing up are on one screen, and the container chooses which one shows first.
An email address and a password are asked for.
Signing up also asks for a name.
Signing up says what the password has to be.
Signing in with Google and with GitHub are both offered.
A pending submission is shown, and cannot be sent twice.
A wrong email address or password is reported in one message for the whole form.
A forgotten password can be reset from here.
The conversation is a log that follows the newest turn.
A message can be written and sent from the bottom of the screen.
A file can be attached to a message.
While a reply is arriving, sending gives way to stopping it.
An empty conversation says what the assistant can help with.
Four headline numbers are shown.
Each headline number says which way it moved since the previous period.
One chart shows requests per day across the period.
The period can be switched between this month and last month.
The layout holds while the numbers load.
A control downloads the period's usage as a file.
The order's standing is shown beside its name.
There is a way back to the list of orders.
The facts about the order are listed as labelled values.
What happened to the order and the team's comments are two lists.
A new comment can be written.
The refund is offered from the top of the page.
Refunding asks for confirmation first.
The confirmation states the amount being refunded, so its words come from the order.
The room and the length are each chosen from a fixed list.
A date is asked for, and a past one cannot be chosen.
A start time is asked for.
The email addresses of the people invited can be entered.
A note for the invitation can be written.
Each required field can say what is wrong beside it.
A summary at the top lists every problem.
One action books the room, and another cancels.
While the booking is being made the screen says so, and it cannot be made twice.
The incidents are shown as the rows of a table.
The list can be sorted.
A search narrows the list.
Two filters narrow the list: one by severity, one by open or resolved.
The screen says how many incidents match.
One control clears every filter at once.
Deleting an incident asks for confirmation first.
The confirmation names the incident being deleted, so its words come from the incident.
No incidents at all and no incident matching the filters are two different messages.
All four steps are shown, with the current one and the finished ones marked.
The name is asked for.
The role is chosen from a short list.
A photo can be added.
Continue is unavailable until the name and the role are filled in.
A control leaves setup, to finish it later.
The settings are in titled sections: general, notifications, access, and a danger zone apart from them.
Each of the five settings says, beside its control, what it changes.
The workspace name can be edited.
The email digest and member invitations are each switched on or off.
The time zone and how often the digest is sent are each chosen from a list.
Deleting the workspace asks for confirmation first.
The confirmation names the workspace, so its words come from the workspace.
